why: p21's sad glossy loop over booming 808s with the 2:40 dropout into a beat switch is moody and cool, while p30 is a bright, cheerful game-chase rush that stays at one volume with no breakdown for two minutes.

Both are flat energetic synth loops, but p27's filtered intro opening into the drop and its 1:50 bass-less breakdown give it more arrival and breathing than p22's harsh wall of the same three-chord loop with only a seven-second drum cut at 2:21.

p23 at least goes near-silent at 0:26 before its full texture sweeps in and drums crash into the climax, a real arrival, while p30 is a cheerful non-stop rush after its 0:20 drop; both sit in the middle, heroic versus bright.

p28's wistful late-night groove that goes muffled at 1:06 and snaps into a heavier half-time stutter is immersive with a real breather, while p22 is a loud game-style rush looping F#m-E-A at one level.
p25 is a warm late-night band groove with a bittersweet lift each cycle and a drumless middle at 1:15, while p29 is a pretty music-box arpeggio that reads as peaceful focus-music wallpaper.

p26 drops into a wistful Dm9 hook after its muffled filter intro and breathes again in the 2:02 breakdown, while p23 is a heroic cinematic build out of a music-box intro whose climax loops one pattern.

p24 has the bigger arrival when the band crashes in at 0:21, but it then sits in a menacing, relentless riff wall, while p28 stays hypnotic and wistful and breathes through its underwater 1:06 breakdown into the heavier half-time section.
p26 has a bittersweet tilt, a muffled-intro drop and a floating 2:02 breakdown before the hook crashes back, while p22 is a flat, harsh game-style loop that barely changes after it slams in at 0:17.

p21's sad, glossy trap loop with drop-outs and a late beat switch has the moody pull this listener wants, while p27 is a polished, energetic Am-F-E arpeggio loop running for a minute at flat level with a happier A-major lift.
p23's near-silent pause at 0:26 before the full ensemble sweeps in gives it an arrival, even if heroic, while p29 never leaves its gentle, pretty harp-like arpeggio beyond soft two-bar swells.
Both are one-level game rushes, but p22's minor 9th voicings, filter intro and 2:21 drum cut give it a slightly cooler, more breathing shape than p30's bright, cheerful major-key chase.
p22 is energetic if flat and slams in hard at 0:17, while p29 is a sweet, peaceful music-box miniature, the kind of gentle-pretty piece this listener likes least.

p24's dark, sad heaviness and the band crashing in after the quiet clean intro fit the loved mood better than p26's bright club hook looping for 70 seconds, though p26 breathes more in its 2:02 breakdown.
p24 delivers a physical arrival when the heavy band crashes in at 0:21 and has a sad, dark weight, while p29 is a gentle, pretty harp loop with almost no change.
p28 is a hypnotic late-night beat with an underwater breakdown into a heavier half-time groove, while p23 is a heroic cinematic build from a music-box intro to a one-loop climax.
p25's warm late-night groove with a bittersweet lift and a drumless development at 1:15 pulls the listener in more than p27's polished energetic arpeggio loop, which runs the same cycle for a minute.

p24's heavy, sad band crashing in after a sparse clean intro has real weight and darkness, while p27 is an energetic but flat arpeggio loop with a happier A-major lift.
p21's sad, glossy trap loop with its 2:40 filtered dropout into a beat switch is moodier and cooler than p26's bright club hook, though p26 has the stronger drop out of its muffled intro.
p25 is a bittersweet late-night groove that breathes through its drumless middle at 1:15, while p30 is a bright, cheerful game-chase rush with no breakdown for over two minutes.
p26 drops into a bittersweet driving hook after its muffled filter intro and relaunches after the 2:02 breakdown, which beats p25's warm but samey bass-led groove whose drumless middle wanders.
p28's hypnotic, darker beat switches to a heavier half-time groove after its underwater breakdown, while p25 is a pleasant warm band groove resting on one bass riff and a lead that holds Eb.
